parsed.summary: Tunisair’s policy and the Montreal Convention allow you to claim reimbursement for reasonable essential‑item expenses when your baggage is delayed, provided you file the claim within the statutory period and include supporting receipts.

steps.when: Within 7 days of receiving your delayed baggage (or as soon as possible if you have not yet received it)
steps.action: Gather all receipts for clothing and other essential items purchased because of the delay, along with your boarding pass, baggage tag, and ID. Keep a copy of the Property Irregularity Report (PIR) you received at the airport.

steps.when: Within 21 days after the baggage was finally delivered to you
steps.action: Submit a written claim to Tunisair’s baggage claims department (via their website, email, or at the airport desk). Include the PIR number, copies of receipts, boarding pass, baggage tag, and a brief statement describing the delay and the items bought.
Follow up with Tunisair if you do not receive acknowledgment within 5 business days. Request confirmation of receipt and an estimated processing time.

steps.when: If the claim is denied or insufficient
steps.action: Escalate the complaint to Tunisair’s customer‑relations office or file a complaint with the Tunisian Civil Aviation Authority. You may also invoke the Montreal Convention (Article 31) for further recourse.
